name: Duke Humanoid V2
dof_breakdown: waist 1, legs 12 (2 x 6), arms 14 (2 x 7), camera gimbals 4 (2 x 2); each parallel gripper adds one more actuated DoF
summary: A 31-DoF quasi-direct-drive humanoid from Duke's General Robotics Lab, built to test perception-aware design. Its two RGB-D cameras sit on independent yaw-pitch gimbals, which the authors report raises visible-reachable workspace coverage from 38% to 97% against the same cameras fixed. The structure is CNC-machined 6061 aluminium and 3D-printed Nylon 12; the authors state that software and hardware designs are open-sourced.
notable: Independently actuated RGB-D cameras raise visible-reachable coverage from 38% to 97% (paper)
